questions.question: Write one line about variability in tourist experiences.
questions.solution_html:
• Variability in tourist experiences refers to how each traveler’s experience can differ due to
  • factors like culture, expectations, service quality, environment, and personal preferences.
  • Decrease in tourist arrivals-Tourists cancel their trips or choose safer destinations
  • leading to a sharp fall in visitor numbers.
  • Preservation of culture-Tourism encourages communities to protect their traditional art, music
  • dance, crafts, and festivals, because tourists are interested in them.
  • Example: Folk dances, handicrafts, and rituals are often revived to attract visitors.
  • Commercialisation of culture-Sometimes traditions are changed or simplified to entertain
  • tourists. This may cause the loss of originality and meaning behind customs.
  • Scuba diving and snorkelling-Tourists explore coral reefs, marine life, and underwater
  • landscapes.
  • Beach relaxation-Sunbathing, swimming, and walking on the shore.
  • Employment generation
  • Coastal activities create jobs for
  • ● Boat operators
  • ● Diving instructors
  • ● Lifeguards
  • ● Hotel and restaurant staff
  • ● Shopkeepers and local artisans
  • Environmental pressure-Overcrowding can damage coral reefs, beaches, and marine
  • ecosystems.
  • Tourists as Demand Creators
  • Tourists create demand for
  • ● Accommodation
  • ● Transport
  • ● Food and beverages
  • ● Attractions and activities
  • ● Shopping and entertainment
  • This demand drives the growth of hotels, restaurants, travel agencies, and local service
  • providers.
  • Enhancing Global Competitiveness
  • a. Differentiation in a competitive world
  • Many countries offer beaches, mountains, and cities, but India stands out with its
  • ● Rich cultural heritage
  • ● Ancient spiritual traditions
  • ● Ayurveda and wellness therapies
  • ● Diverse landscapes ranging from the Himalayas to coastal regions
  • ● Vibrant festivals and cuisines
  • Promoting these unique products helps India stand apart in a crowded global market.
  • b. Boosting India’s international image
  • Showcasing world-class attractions such as
  • ● Taj Mahal
  • ● Varanasi
  • ● Kerala backwaters
  • ● Rann of Kutch
  • ● Wildlife sanctuaries
  • creates a strong identity and positions India as a must-visit global destination.
  • c. Attracting niche and high-spending tourists
  • Promoting specialised tourism products—like adventure tourism, medical tourism, heritage
  • tourism, eco-tourism, and culinary tourism—helps attract travellers willing to spend more
  • thereby increasing foreign exchange earnings.
questions.final_answer: Option Differentiation in a competitive world
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: List two ways to promote sustainable tourism in desert areas.
questions.solution_html:
• List two ways to promote sustainable tourism in desert areas.
  • ● Use eco-friendly infrastructure, such as solar-powered facilities and water-efficient
  • systems to reduce environmental impact.
  • ● Encourage community-based tourism, where local people manage tours and activities
  • helping conserve the desert ecosystem and support local livelihoods.
  • A pilgrimage trip to Varanasi
  • Includes: train journey + accommodation + temple visits + local transport + guide.
  • → Many services combined into one travel experience.
  • Economic losses-Hotels, restaurants, transport services, travel agencies, and local
  • businesses suffer because fewer tourists means less income.
  • Economic support for cultural activities-Local people earn money by performing traditional
  • arts, selling handmade products, or organising cultural shows. This gives financial value to their
  • traditions.
  • Change in lifestyle-Exposure to modern lifestyles of tourists can influence local
  • people—especially youth—to adopt new fashion, food habits, and values.This may lead to a
  • shift away from traditional ways of living.
  • Surfing and windsurfing-Coastal areas with strong waves attract surfers from around the
  • world.
  • Cruise trips and boat tours-Short cruises, sunset tours, and island-hopping packages.
  • Growth of local businesses
  • Tourists spend money on
  • ● Food and beverages
  • ● Handicrafts
  • ● Local transportation
  • ● Water-sport equipment rentals
  • This boosts income for small and medium businesses.
  • Seasonal dependency-Coastal tourism mostly peaks during certain seasons; income
  • becomes unstable during off-season.
  • Tourists Influence Destination Development
  • Tourist preferences determine how destinations evolve. For example
  • ● If tourists prefer adventure activities, the destination develops trekking routes, water
  • sports, or adventure parks.
  • ● If tourists are interested in culture and heritage, the destination invests in museums
  • cultural shows, and preservation of monuments.
  • Driving Sustainable Economic Growth
  • a. Generating employment and livelihoods
  • Tourism is one of India’s largest employment generators. Promoting unique tourism products
  • ● Creates jobs in hospitality, transport, handicrafts, and services
  • ● Provides income opportunities in rural and tribal areas
  • ● Encourages local entrepreneurship
  • This supports inclusive and balanced regional development.
  • b. Boosting local economies by supporting crafts and traditions
  • India’s unique cultural tourism promotes
  • ● Handicrafts
  • ● Traditional arts
  • ● Local cuisines
  • ● Communities involved in heritage conservation
  • This helps preserve traditions that might otherwise disappear while providing steady income to
  • artisans.
  • c. Encouraging investment and infrastructure development
  • When India promotes its world-class tourism assets, it attracts both domestic and foreign
  • investment. This leads to
  • ● Better roads, airports, sanitation, and accommodation
  • ● Increased safety and tourist-friendly services
  • These improvements benefit both tourists and local residents.
questions.final_answer: Option Generating employment and livelihoods
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: List any two roles of District Tourism Authorities.
questions.solution_html:
• List any two roles of District Tourism Authorities.
  • ● Planning and developing local tourism facilities and attractions within the district.
  • ● Promoting and regulating tourism activities to ensure safety, quality, and sustainable
  • practices.
  • Loss of jobs-Many people working in tourism—guides, drivers, hotel staff
  • shopkeepers—may lose their jobs due to reduced tourist flow.
  • Cultural exchange-Tourists and locals interact, leading to an exchange of ideas, languages
  • and knowledge.This improves understanding and openness in the community.
  • Negative influences
  • Cultural conflicts-Differences in behaviour, dress codes, or social norms between tourists and
  • locals can create misunderstandings or cultural tensions.
  • Jet skiing and parasailing-High-speed water sports that attract young and adventure-seeking
  • travellers.
  • Coastal cultural events-Beach festivals, seafood fairs, and music events attract more visitors.
  • Infrastructure development-Demand for tourism leads to improvements in
  • ● Roads
  • ● Ports
  • ● Safety services
  • ● Hospitality facilities
  • This benefits both tourists and local residents.
  • Rising living costs-Tourist hotspots sometimes become expensive for local residents due to
  • rising land and food prices.
  • Tourists Impact the Local Economy
  • Tourist spending supports
  • ● Local businesses
  • ● Employment
  • ● Community income
  • ● Government revenue (taxes, entry fees)
  • Supporting Environmental and Cultural Sustainability
  • a. Preservation of natural resources
  • Promoting eco-friendly tourism products like wildlife tourism, Himalayan trekking routes, and
  • coastal tourism encourages
  • ● Conservation of forests, rivers, and wildlife
  • ● Regulation of tourist activities
  • ● Responsible travel practices
  • This protects fragile ecosystems.
  • b. Conservation of heritage sites
  • When heritage tourism is promoted, the government and communities invest more in
  • ● Restoration of monuments
  • ● Protection of archaeological sites
  • ● Maintenance of cultural landscapes
  • This ensures India’s heritage is preserved for future generations.
  • c. Promoting responsible tourism behaviour
  • Highlighting India’s unique products encourages
  • ● Community-based tourism
  • ● Low-impact travel
  • ● Respect for local culture and environment
  • This reduces negative impacts often caused by mass tourism.
questions.final_answer: Option Preservation of natural resources
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is meant by eco-tourism in mountain regions?
questions.solution_html:
• Eco-tourism in mountain regions means travelling to hills or mountain areas in a responsible
  • and environmentally friendly way.
  • Negative image of the destination-Once a place is labelled as unsafe, it becomes difficult
  • to rebuild its reputation. This long-term negative image discourages future travellers.
  • Decline of traditional occupations-As tourism grows, people may leave traditional jobs (like
  • farming or handicrafts) for tourism-related work, causing weakening of old practices.
  • Deep-sea fishing-Tourists go on guided fishing trips in the open sea.
  • Wildlife watching-Watching dolphins, turtles, and coastal birds provides a calm leisure
  • experience.
  • Impact on Local Economies
  • Positive Impacts
  • Increased government revenue-Taxes from hotels, cruises, water sports, and entry fees
  • increase government income, which can be used for further development.
  • Negative Impacts (brief)
  • Tourists Influence Environmental Conditions
  • Tourist behaviour affects the natural environment
  • Positive behaviour
  • ● Following eco-friendly practices
  • ● Avoiding littering
  • ● Respecting wildlife
  • ● Supporting conservation initiatives
  • This helps preserve the destination for future generations.
  • Negative behaviour
  • ● Overcrowding
  • ● Waste generation
  • ● Pollution of beaches, forests, or heritage sites
  • ● Damage to natural resources
  • Such behaviours lead to environmental degradation and loss of attraction value.
  • Strengthening India’s Soft Power and Global Presence
  • Tourism promotion enhances India’s global visibility by
  • ● Strengthening cultural diplomacy
  • ● Showcasing Indian values of hospitality (“Atithi Devo Bhava”)
  • ● Building cultural relationships with other nations
  • A strong global tourism image contributes to India’s overall international influence.
questions.final_answer: A strong global tourism image contributes to India’s overall international influence
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.solution_html:

  • sectors of the economy.

  • income for the economy. As money circulates from tourism businesses to suppliers and
  • workers, it generates employment, demand, investment, and economic development in many
  • sectors—demonstrating tourism's wide-reaching importance to national and local economies.

questions.question: Why are attractions considered the motivators of travel?
questions.solution_html:
• Attractions motivate people to travel because they draw tourists’ attention and give them a
  • reason to visit a destination.
  • ● Attractions create interest and desire to travel
  • Tourists decide to visit a destination because they want to see or experience its
  • attractions—such as beaches, mountains, historical monuments, festivals, or wildlife.
  • ● They give purpose to the trip
  • Without attractions, people would have no specific reason to visit a place. Attractions
  • provide the main purpose, excitement, and meaning for the journey.
questions.final_answer: provide the main purpose, excitement, and meaning for the journey
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of a composite tourism product with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• A composite tourism product is a complete travel experience created by the combination of
  • many different services used by a tourist.When a person travels, they need several services
  • ● Transport
  • ● Accommodation
  • ● Food
  • ● Attractions
  • ● Activities
  • ● Guides
  • ● Local transport
  • ● Shopping
  • All these together form a composite tourism product.
  • Examples- 1.A holiday package to Goa
  • Includes: flight + hotel + meals + sightseeing + beach activities.
  • → All these elements together form one composite tourism product.
questions.final_answer: → All these elements together form one composite tourism product
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
